subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` stay private to owner-scoped Browser/Ollama paths, or may it become part of the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` contract?
rationale: The current PR's one-line import cannot compile without either exposing a private managed-proxy bypass helper publicly or choosing a different package-resolution repair, and that boundary choice is not safe for automation to infer.

options.title: Preserve Private Owner-Scoped Access
options.body: Keep the helper private and repair packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the owner-scoped internal surface or another narrow bundled-plugin path.

options.title: Approve Public SSRF Runtime Export
options.body: Promote the helper into `ssrf-runtime` only with explicit SDK/security approval, docs or guardrail updates, and package smoke proof.

options.title: Use A Canonical Sibling PR
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers choose a broader sibling branch as the canonical repair for the same package-subpath regression.

recommendation.title: Preserve Private Owner-Scoped Access
recommendation.body: Keep the helper private and repair packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the owner-scoped internal surface or another narrow bundled-plugin path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about package/private SDK boundary policy, and this handle has direct history on private SDK declaration packaging.
